diagrams.title: From One Injured Family to a Settlement Matrix
diagrams.subtitle: How a mass tort becomes an MDL docket, step by step

stages.label: Mine single-family intake
stages.detail: The baby formula litigation started with one mother who lost a child and went to a firm that did not do mass torts; Stewart & Stewart turned one pressure cooker burn into a known seal-issue pattern.

stages.label: Front-load the medical records
stages.detail: By the time defendants get medical authorizations, Joseph Lyon's firm has already gathered most of the critical records that substantiate the case.

stages.label: Clear the JPML numerosity trigger
stages.detail: Searcy Law looks for 20 to 50 cases with hundreds or thousands expected; some MDLs form on fewer than 20, some petitions are denied, and venue cannot be banked on from oral argument.

stages.label: Fund leadership through a common fund
stages.detail: Executive committee of 4-5 and a steering committee of 2-3 up to 20 self-fund document review, depositions and experts; confirm co-counsel funding before committing.

stages.label: Bellwether pool sets the settlement matrix
stages.detail: Dolman Law Group describes 50 to 100 claims, maybe a few more, pulled from thousands to gather records and pick representative bellwether cases.

diagrams.caption: A mass tort is the injury; the MDL is the payout vehicle where each plaintiff keeps an individual lawsuit after consolidated pretrial work.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Thresholds and committee sizes are attributed practitioner claims and vary by docket. Roberts tells MDL clients they each get their own trial, while Dolman says very few cases are ever tried.
diagrams.note: Sources: Searcy Law Video (yIQ0NYXRsmQ), Dolman Law Group (qGQGuFYFCF8), Attorney Joseph Lyon (nUl1KZ2z_es), CW33 KDAF (hSl_yaMfnv0), Stewart & Stewart Attorneys (4iH4c_z7Iw0), Roberts & Roberts Law Firm (XubmYzsLJEw).

diagrams.title: Where the Raw Lead Leaks
diagrams.subtitle: Intake quality versus retainer reality, in percent of raw leads

stages.label: Raw leads entering intake
stages.conversion: Starting pool before congruence checks and TrustedForm
stages.detail: Case Works runs email and phone congruence checks plus TrustedForm so bad leads die before workup, the largest cost in the chain.

stages.label: Qualified on a working intake floor
stages.detail: Alert Communications benchmark from a 425-staff intake operation that adjusts staffing every 15 minutes.

stages.label: Qualified on a broken intake floor
stages.detail: Alert Communications contrasts its floor with broken intake that converts only 20% to 40%.

stages.label: Retainers on one niche tort
stages.detail: John Casto reports one niche tort converting at 16% with payouts of a couple thousand dollars.

stages.label: Typical raw-lead retainers
stages.detail: Casto's typical conversion; a DQ filter doubled CPL with no lift. Devin Downey measured about 30% attrition from 2020 to 2024 on signed cases.

diagrams.caption: The signed retainer is the wrong finish line; cost per retained, settlement-ready case is the number that matters.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stages combine separate practitioner benchmarks on one percent scale and are not a single measured cohort. Signed-case CPA spans $300 to six grand or more.
diagrams.note: Sources: Advanced Affiliate with John Casto (Tt2FvNxVuCs), Alert Communications (PJEVefyQCxA), Case Works with Devin Downey (My_I0OLHPXc), Blue Sky Legal (n9AQhSIMkNg).

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before a Toxic-Exposure File Counts
diagrams.subtitle: Proof, exposure, reachability and opt-out paperwork

nodes.question: Do medical records ordered across providers and years prove the injury?
nodes.fail_action: Hold the file; belief of exposure or a general PFAS-linked condition is not enough (Napoli Shkolnik).

nodes.question: Is exposure documented via firefighter work history or residency mapped by PWSID or ZIP code?
nodes.fail_action: Do not count the file; expect deficiency rounds (King Law has seen four).

nodes.question: Is client contact info current and an estate rep lined up?
nodes.fail_action: Chase moved and deceased claimants now; talc firms are working toward a 95% threshold and excluded clients face an uphill fight.

nodes.question: For Roundup opt-outs, is there an original wet signature with ID inside 90 days?
nodes.pass_next: Enroll and budget at least 1.5 years to first funds
nodes.fail_action: No DocuSign; a missed window sweeps the file into the class.

diagrams.caption: Toxic-exposure dockets pay only after defendants can count their liability; the AFFF MDL drew 131,000 filings and was scrubbed toward 80,000 to 90,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is a sequencing of separately reported practitioner checks. Settlement lag of at least 1.5 years is Michael Stanisci's rule of thumb.
diagrams.note: Sources: King Law (aOm5hBG6t9s), Napoli Shkolnik (S1VC15_WonY), Jon and Marc (NHmq2W3F_do, 3Qxw8dtCCns), Steve Smith on Cut to the Chase Network (-H3O5pPP-XA), Michael Stanisci (_qBek9AFPiI).

diagrams.title: The Law-Firm MSO Blueprint
diagrams.subtitle: Non-lawyer operations spun out, legal judgment kept inside the firm

center.headcount: All non-lawyer staff, plus equipment, IP and founder likeness
center.focus: Leased back for a fixed monthly or cost-plus fee with 10-15% markups, validated by a third-party fairness opinion

spokes.kpi: Keeps lawyers, engagement letters, trust accounts, hiring, case selection and settlement; mind the UnitedLex improper-control finding
Fee re-priced forward-looking only, on a roughly annual cadence
Buy in at 5x to roll up PI firms at 35% margins; law firms trade at 4-8x versus about 15x for accounting
Burford funds 6-8% of reviewed cases at mid-20s IRRs; 39 funders committed $2.8B in 2025

diagrams.caption: Spin operations into the MSO, lease them back, and keep every legal decision with the lawyers.
diagrams.assumptions_note: MSO fees must never be a percentage of profits or revenue. Practitioners disagree on mass-tort cash-flow unpredictability and true portfolio diversification.
diagrams.note: Sources: Holland & Knight's Trisha Rich and Josh Port on Confido Legal (5TjsKzLtyc4), Joe Prencipe, Chris Bogart on TALKSONLAW (1kAfGIkF10g), The National Law Review (9teRv9eFpEc), Jon and Marc (U2xFBBUm_IU).

diagrams.title: Four-Step MSO and ABS Setup Roadmap
diagrams.subtitle: Entity split, fee structure, buyer vetting and Arizona compliance

weeks.title: Split the two companies
weeks.deliverable: Licensed professional entity owns the practice; an MSO anyone can own is linked by a management service agreement
weeks.gate: Non-lawyers never practice law, mirroring the CPOM rule Jackson LLP describes

weeks.title: Set the MSA fee
weeks.deliverable: Flat monthly fee or cost plus fair margin
weeks.gate: Any percentage of law-firm revenue is a no-go (Holt Law)

weeks.title: Vet the buyer
weeks.deliverable: Benchmark offers against 6-8x profit market multiples versus a 4x offer
weeks.gate: Walk from any pitch that controlling intake means controlling the firm; Shelton rejected about 90% of 70-plus PE-backed MSOs

weeks.title: File for the Arizona ABS track
weeks.deliverable: Compliance lawyer with management experience, 10% ownership disclosure, Arizona-admitted lawyer handling intake and records
weeks.gate: Plan for approval of about 4 months, now 6-8 months

diagrams.caption: Healthcare and law-firm practitioners describe the same split between the licensed entity and the management company.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week labels sequence the setup and do not reflect regulator timelines; Rodriguez ran March to August while others report 6 to 8 month queues.
diagrams.note: Sources: Jackson LLP Healthcare Lawyers (wUqthLNx6Ro), Holt Law (DNk78wbKy5s), Frederick Shelton on Ten Golden Rules (I4F5OYZQJuU), Lynda Shely on Law Leaders (Tvn12qG9i5s), The Heart of Law Podcast (poe1CAsUc4U, OdPOa3osKC0).
